newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee widens falls, seen consolidating.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee widens falls, seen consolidating.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures ended midsession with modest losses amid light dealings in consolidation to recent advance.
"It's moving sideways, perhaps in correction to the recent rally," said one traders. But others said the market could vault higher again if the New York arabica futures resumed their upward climb.
The market headed sharply lower at the start. Most prices clawed back to session's highs towards the morning close but still down from Wednesday's finish.
Benchmark March shed $18 at $1,517 a tonne after its earlier slide was stalled at $1,500.
Technically, the market's outlook remained constructive, analysts said. Resistance is pegged at the recent high at $1,630 a tonne basis March while support was seen at $1,424.
News Colombia's leading independent coffee growers' association declared a moratorium on debt payments came after both London and New York markets were closed.
Growers said the move was part of a campaign of "civil disobedience" aimed at improving the lot of cash-strapped farmers.

The radical decision, which would affect about $200 million in past-due loans owed to the state-run Caja Agraria bank and Banco Cafetero -- a bank partly owned by the government- affiliated National Coffee Growers' Federation -- was adopted at a meeting of the independent Unidad Cafetera Nacional in the western city of Pereira.
One London trader said: "It is an internal payments problem between the growers and the banks. I don't think it would affect the outflow of coffee into the market."
Traders said the news had no immediate influence on prices.
In physicals, traders said the market was virtually at a standstill this week as futures prices took a dip.
However, the steady differentials continued to deter roaster interest.
"Roasters who don't need to buy coffee are willing to wait for much lower prices," said one trader. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
